name: Sidon
overview: Sidon is a male figure identified in Scripture as the son of Canaan. He is noted primarily for his lineage, being a descendant of Canaan, which situates him within the early genealogies recorded in Genesis. There is no additional tribal affiliation or further personal details provided in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Sidon appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:15. There is no specific meaning or divine origin attributed to the name in the biblical record, so it is presented simply as the personal name of this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Sidon is recorded as the son of Canaan, establishing his place in the family line descending from Noah through Ham. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide further family details or connections for Sidon.
scriptureSignificance: Sidon's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his position as a son of Canaan, contributing to the genealogical framework that outlines the origins of various peoples following the Flood. His mention helps to trace the descendants of Canaan, who are often associated with the inhabitants of the land that would later be significant in Israel's history. While the text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, Sidon's inclusion underscores the biblical emphasis on lineage and the fulfillment of God's sovereign plan through generations.
